thread:
rohan: Heads up — ap-southeast1 GPU pools failing to get new pods. Lots of nodes in SchedulingDisabled because kubelet marks them NotReady after local NVMe write errors.
olga: Ugh. Any dmesg or nvme SMARTs?
rohan: Pasted latest dmesg from one host:\n\n```"[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0xabcdef failed err 5
[ 1234.568001] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567 op 1
[ 1234.568210] scrubber: detected heavy write stall from background_replicator"```\n\nrohan: This started ~2h after we enabled cross-region async snapshot replication for scratch volumes (replicator v2). Suspect replication storms hitting ephemeral NVMe.
nate: Replicator config default is pretty aggressive. Can you check current rate limiter? (cc @jia)
jia: Checking — looks like replicator rate was bumped to unlimited by the rollout yesterday in ap-southeast1 to speed up backfills. That's likely it.
rohan: Jobs affected are all GPU batch pods, they do small sync writes during model cache warmup — write tail + replicator = IOPS storm causing device timeouts and then kernel marks device degraded.
olga: Any immediate mitigation we can do to unblock GPU provisioning? We have a few customer jobs stuck.
rohan: Short term: cordon a subset of hosts and restart kubelet after cleaning NVMe queue, and throttle replicator back to 50MB/s for the region. I'll open a patch for replicator.
nate: +1 on throttling. Also maybe move model-cache writes to tmpfs for warmup to avoid hitting NVMe until replicator finishes.
jia: I'll roll a quick rate-limit change: `replicator.rate_limit=50MB/s` for ap-southeast1. Doing a staged roll now.
janitor-bot: scheduled job "scratch-scrub" next run in 6m, current backlog 4200 files — high concurrency = more IO.
rohan: Can we stagger scrub concurrency? That backlog + replicator = bad combo.
jia: Changing scrub concurrency to 2 for ap-southeast1 in 2m.
sre-oncall: For hosts already degraded, plan for replacement: Cordon -> drain -> reprovision local NVMe (trim + fsck) -> uncordon. Do we lose pods if we drain now? Some stateful ML trainers store model cache on local disk.
olga: For critical GPU jobs, we should evict non-critical pods first (batch-preemptible). I'll prepare a pod-affinity drain list.
rohan: Action items: 1) Jia throttles replicator (in flight) — done? 2) Jia reduces scrub concurrency — done? 3) Nate, Olga to cordon and drain 6 worst hosts, run `nvme format` only after we ensure no persistent data, else `fstrim` + e2fsck. 4) Rohan to add a postmortem ticket and cost estimate for cross-region replication cost / increased wear.
jia: Replicator rate roll complete to 50MB/s in ap-southeast1. Monitoring IOPS now.
janitor-bot: alert: iops_ap_southeast1 avg dropped from 35k -> 7k after change.
nate: Starting cordon/drain on node gnode-ap-s1-047. Drain command: `kubectl drain gnode-ap-s1-047 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will evict non-crit pods only.
rohan: Remember to set `--pod-selector='!ml-critical'` so we don't evict critical trainers.
olga: Doing node maintenance now. I'll run `dmesg | tail -n 50` after drain and attach.
olga: Post-maintenance dmesg shows fewer IO errors, nvme SMART pre-fail counters still elevated but not catastrophic.
rohan: For follow-up: propose default replicator cap per region, safer scrub scheduling (windowed), and a guideline to use tmpfs for cache warmup on GPU nodes. I'll draft RFC.
jia: Filing RFC draft now. Also adding automated kill-switch: if NVMe write latency > 200ms for 5m, pause replicator.
nate: Thx. Quick cost note: slower replication increases egress time for snapshots but reduces risk of device replacement costs. Put numbers in the PM ticket.
rohan: OK — keeping this thread for updates. If anything regresses ping here or @sre-oncall. :thumbsup:
